Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with

A study [39] with 11623 middle-aged Chinese individuals
categorized three groups based on CRP levels (< 1.0, 1.0-3.0, and > 3.0) and obtained the result that
the HR for all-cause mortality in the > 3.0 group was 2.64 (95% CI: 1.74, 4.01).
...
Conclusion
Our analyses indicated that high CRP concentrations are likely to be a prospective factor predicting
death among the oldest old adults.
CRP may be more useful clinically in identifying higher risk
populations for all-cause mortality.
